newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Alcoa Q3 net falls.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Alcoa Q3 net falls.

text.p: Alcoa on Friday said third quarter net was $139.9 million, or $0.77 a share, before a charge of $65.5 million, or $0.38 a share. In 1995, earnings in the quarter were $226.4 million, or $1.27 a share.
It said earnings were reduced by a steel strike in Cleveland and marking to market certain aluminum commodity contracts.
This is the full text of the company's news release.

PITTSBURGH--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 4, 1996--Alcoa today announced third quarter 1996 earnings of $133.9 million, or 77 cents per common share, before a special after-tax charge of $65.5 million ($115.1 pre-tax), or 38 cents per share, for the layoff provision and equipment write-down announced earlier. After the charge, the company had net income of $68.4 million, or 39 cents per share. Third quarter 1995 net income was a third quarter record at $226.4 million, or $1.27 per share.

Third quarter 1996 earnings were negatively affected by the strike at the Cleveland forging plant by $6.5 million, or 4 cents per share, and also included after-tax losses of $16 million, or 9 cents per share, resulting from marking to market certain aluminum commodity contracts. The company enters into these commodity contracts to lock in conversion margins for fabricated product businesses, and to have its primary metal units at market prices at all times. Of these losses, $3.4 million, or 2 cents per share, is attributable to fabricated product sales contracts that were delivered during the third quarter and $12.6 million, or 7 cents per share, is related to fabricated product sales contracts that will be shipped in future quarters.

For the first nine months of 1996, earnings were $484.3 million, or $2.77 per share, before after-tax charges of $105.5 million, or $.61 per share. This compares with $639.6 million, or $3.58 per share, for the 1995 nine-month period.

After charges, net income for the 1996 nine-month period was $378.8 million, or $2.16 per share. The year-to-date charges include the layoff provision mentioned earlier and a second quarter charge of $40.0 million for closing the company's ceramic packaging operations in California.

Revenues for the 1996 third quarter were $3.2 billion compared with $3.3 billion for the 1995 third quarter. Aluminum product shipments were 717,000 metric tons (mt) compared with 655,000 mt in the year-ago quarter.
Year-to-date, revenues were $9.8 billion compared with $9.4 billion for the first nine months of 1995, while shipments were 2,094,000 mt compared with 1,936,000 mt.

The quarter and year-to-date results compared with 1995 reflect lower realized prices for aluminum ingot and several fabricated products including rigid container sheet; higher costs for raw materials; and, losses from marking to market certain aluminum commodity contracts.
Excluding the charges, return on shareholders' equity for the first nine months of 1996, annualized, was 14.4%, compared with 20.1% for the year-ago period.
Alcoa is the world's largest producer of aluminum. The company has 170 operating locations in 28 countries. Financial and operating data for Alcoa and its subsidiaries follow.
